prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable unit 69px · widest one-line content 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable unit 66px · widest one-line content 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable unit 68px · widest one-line content 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable unit 42px · widest one-line content 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable unit 68px · widest one-line content 1035px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 720px wide (column widths sum to at most 719px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 720px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Several designers worked independently on this table. You see their final layouts, anonymised as Layout P, Layout Q, Layout R, Layout S, Layout T, Layout U, in that order after the overview: Layout P, Layout Q, Layout R, Layout S, Layout T, Layout U.
Measured facts:
Layout P: column widths [110, 130, 120, 90, 269] px · table 720×720 px · row heights [60, 129, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout Q: column widths [105, 120, 120, 90, 284] px · table 720×697 px · row heights [60, 129, 83, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout R: column widths [110, 120, 115, 90, 284] px · table 720×697 px · row heights [60, 129, 83, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout S: column widths [115, 125, 125, 90, 264] px · table 720×720 px · row heights [60, 129, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout T: column widths [110, 115, 115, 90, 289] px · table 720×697 px · row heights [60, 129, 83, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout U: column widths [105, 130, 130, 90, 264] px · table 720×720 px · row heights [60, 129, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)

Compare them side by side. For each layout name its strengths, its faults and the spatial logic behind it (how it distributes space and why). Do not just pick a winner: you may combine the strengths of several layouts, propose something new, or overturn all of them. Propose up to 3 new designs that you expect to be better than every layout shown; if you believe one shown layout cannot be improved, say so in "best" and propose fewer or none.
